question: Is there free anti-rabies vaccine for dogs from the government?
answer:
Often, yes. Section 6 of RA 9482 tells the Department of Agriculture to lead free anti-rabies vaccination of dogs, with priority for high-risk, low-income areas. LGUs must fund vaccines and run registration and vaccination (Section 7).

Executive Order No. 84 (1999) also calls for mass dog vaccination with free vaccines every March, Rabies Awareness Month.

Schedules differ by place, so watch for announcements from your barangay or ask your city or municipal veterinary office about the next free vaccination drive.

question: When is Rabies Awareness Month in the Philippines?
answer:
March. Executive Order No. 84, signed in 1999, declared March of every year as Rabies Awareness Month. It calls for a nationwide rabies information drive and mass dog vaccination with free vaccines.

The implementing rules of RA 9482 also mark March as Rabies Awareness Month, and September 28 as World Rabies Day.

Many LGUs hold free vaccination and pet registration activities in March, so it's a good time to update your pet's shots.

question: Do I need to keep my dog's vaccination card?
answer:
Yes. Section 5 of RA 9482 requires owners to keep a registration card that records all of their dog's vaccinations. The implementing rules say the card should show the registration number, the dog's description, and vaccination details.

Keep it safe because you may need it:
- To show your dog is registered and vaccinated if asked by the LGU
- To get a BAI shipping permit when travelling with your pet
- If your dog bites someone and its rabies status is checked

Taking a photo of the card is a handy backup.

question: Is it legal to sell or eat dog meat in the Philippines?
answer:
No. RA 9482 bans the trade of dog meat. LGUs must enforce this ban (Section 7).

Under Section 11, anyone caught trading dog meat faces a fine of at least P5,000 per dog and 1 to 4 years in prison. The same penalty applies to using electrocution to put dogs to sleep. Foreigners who break these rules are deported after serving their sentence.

Killing dogs for food is also not among the allowed reasons for killing animals under the Animal Welfare Act (RA 8485, Section 6).

question: A dog bit me (nakagat ako ng aso). What should I do?
answer:
Act right away, even if the dog looks healthy.

- Wash the wound with soap and running water for about 15 minutes
- Don't put garlic or other home remedies on it, and don't rely on "tandok" or "tambal" healers
- Go to the nearest Animal Bite Treatment Center (ABTC) or Animal Bite Center promptly for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)
- Finish the full vaccine schedule the health workers give you

Don't wait for symptoms. Once rabies symptoms appear, it is almost always fatal. If the dog has an owner, they should report the bite and have the dog observed for 14 days.
source: DOH Bicol CHD, https://bicol.doh.gov.ph/news-releases/doh-bicol-chd-urges-immediate-treatment-after-animal-bites-scratches-responsible-pet-ownership-key-to-rabies-prevention/; WHO Rabies fact sheet, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies; IRR of RA 9482 (AO No. 01 s. 2008), Rule 5(e), https://dev.lawyerly.ph/laws/56761

question: My cat scratched me. Do I need to go to the animal bite center?
answer:
Yes, it's safest to get checked. Rabies can spread through scratches as well as bites, and cats can carry rabies.

- Wash the scratch with soap and running water for about 15 minutes
- Go to the nearest Animal Bite Treatment Center (ABTC) promptly so a health worker can decide if you need post-exposure prophylaxis

The WHO counts even minor scratches without bleeding as an exposure that may need vaccination. Don't wait to see if the cat gets sick first.
source: DOH Bicol CHD, https://bicol.doh.gov.ph/news-releases/doh-bicol-chd-urges-immediate-treatment-after-animal-bites-scratches-responsible-pet-ownership-key-to-rabies-prevention/; WHO Rabies fact sheet, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies

question: Do I still need anti-rabies shots if the dog that bit me is vaccinated?
answer:
Still go to an Animal Bite Treatment Center (ABTC) promptly after washing the wound. The health workers there will look at the bite and the dog's vaccination record and decide what treatment you need.

Don't skip the visit or wait for the dog to finish its 14-day observation first. DOH offices urge immediate consultation after any bite or scratch, because rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms appear.

Bring the dog's vaccination card or a photo of it if you can.
source: DOH Bicol CHD, https://bicol.doh.gov.ph/news-releases/doh-bicol-chd-urges-immediate-treatment-after-animal-bites-scratches-responsible-pet-ownership-key-to-rabies-prevention/; WHO Rabies fact sheet, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies; IRR of RA 9482 (AO No. 01 s. 2008), Rule 5(e), https://dev.lawyerly.ph/laws/56761

question: How is rabies spread?
answer:
Rabies spreads through the saliva of an infected animal, mostly through:

- Bites
- Scratches
- Saliva getting into open wounds, eyes, nose or mouth

Dogs cause up to 99% of human rabies cases worldwide, according to the WHO. In the Philippines, the DOH said 45% of rabies cases in 2024 came from the saliva of household pets.

Touching or feeding an animal, or a lick on unbroken skin, is not considered an exposure. Still, wash the area with soap and water.
source: WHO Rabies fact sheet, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies; DOH data reported by Inquirer (15 March 2025), https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2044154/rabies-cases-in-ph-almost-doubled-between-2020-and-2024

question: Can rabies be cured?
answer:
Once symptoms show, rabies is almost always fatal, in both people and animals. That's why acting before symptoms appear is so important.

Rabies is fully preventable:
- After a bite or scratch, wash the wound well and get post-exposure prophylaxis at an Animal Bite Treatment Center right away
- Vaccinate your dogs and cats every year

In people, symptoms can appear about one week to one year after exposure, usually after 2 to 3 months. So don't wait to see if you feel sick.
source: WHO Rabies fact sheet, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies; DOH Bicol CHD, https://bicol.doh.gov.ph/news-releases/doh-bicol-chd-urges-immediate-treatment-after-animal-bites-scratches-responsible-pet-ownership-key-to-rabies-prevention/; DOH data reported by Inquirer (15 March 2025), https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2044154/rabies-cases-in-ph-almost-doubled-between-2020-and-2024

question: What are the signs of rabies in a dog or cat?
answer:
The DOH lists these signs of rabies in animals:

- Change in behavior
- Aggressive behavior
- Excessive drooling
- Paralysis
- Fear of water

You can't confirm rabies just by looking at an animal; only a lab test can. If your pet shows these signs, keep away from its saliva, keep it confined, and call your vet or city or municipal veterinary office right away. If it bit or scratched anyone, they should go to an Animal Bite Treatment Center.
source: DOH data reported by Inquirer (15 March 2025), https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2044154/rabies-cases-in-ph-almost-doubled-between-2020-and-2024; IRR of RA 9482 (AO No. 01 s. 2008), Rule 9(2), https://dev.lawyerly.ph/laws/56761

question: Can cats get rabies too, or only dogs?
answer:
Cats can get rabies and pass it to people through bites and scratches. Rabies can infect all mammals.

The Anti-Rabies Act (RA 9482) mainly talks about dogs, but DOH offices urge owners to vaccinate both dogs and cats against rabies regularly and not let them roam freely. The national campaign theme is "Rabies-free na pusa't aso, kaligtasan ng pamilyang Pilipino."

Ask your vet about your cat's yearly anti-rabies shot, and treat any cat bite or scratch seriously.
source: WHO Rabies fact sheet, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies; DOH Bicol CHD, https://bicol.doh.gov.ph/news-releases/doh-bicol-chd-urges-immediate-treatment-after-animal-bites-scratches-responsible-pet-ownership-key-to-rabies-prevention/; DOH Ilocos CHD, https://ro1.doh.gov.ph/doh-ilocos-pushes-for-community-action-to-stop-the-spread-of-rabies-in-pangasinan/

question: Is anti-rabies treatment for people free?
answer:
Under Section 6 of RA 9482, the DOH must provide post-exposure treatment for bite victims at minimum cost, and free pre-exposure shots for high-risk workers. Free routine shots are also given to schoolchildren aged 5 to 14 in high-risk areas (Section 4).

Costs can still differ between government and private Animal Bite Treatment Centers, so ask your local health center or ABTC. Never skip treatment because of cost. And if a dog bit you, its owner is required by law to pay your medical expenses (Section 5).
source: Republic Act No. 9482, Sections 4, 5 and 6, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2007/ra_9482_2007.html

question: What counts as animal cruelty under Philippine law?
answer:
Under Section 6 of the Animal Welfare Act (RA 8485, as amended by RA 10631), it is illegal to:

- Torture any animal
- Neglect to give an animal enough care, food or shelter, or otherwise maltreat it
- Use dogs or horses in dogfights or horsefights
- Kill an animal other than livestock like cattle, pigs, goats, poultry and rabbits, except in cases the law allows
- Use animals in research not approved by the Committee on Animal Welfare

Abandoning a pet without arranging its care is also treated as maltreatment (Section 7, added by RA 10631).
source: Republic Act No. 10631, Sections 6 and 7, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2013/ra_10631_2013.html; Republic Act No. 8485, Section 6, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1998/ra_8485_1998.html

question: Is it illegal to abandon my pet?
answer:
Yes. RA 10631, which amended the Animal Welfare Act, added a rule against abandoning animals.

- Leaving your pet, for good or even for a while, without a good reason and without arranging for its care counts as maltreatment
- If abandonment leads to the animal suffering or dying, the owner faces the maximum penalty

If you can no longer care for your pet, look for a new home or ask a rescue group or shelter for help instead of leaving it on the street.
source: Republic Act No. 10631, Section 7 (new Section 7 of RA 8485), https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2013/ra_10631_2013.html

question: What's the penalty for animal cruelty in the Philippines?
answer:
Section 9 of the Animal Welfare Act, as amended by RA 10631, sets penalties after conviction:

- Animal dies: 1 year, 6 months and 1 day to 2 years in prison, and/or a fine up to P100,000
- Animal survives but is severely injured and can't survive without human help: 1 year and 1 day to 1 year and 6 months, and/or up to P50,000
- Other cruelty or neglect: 6 months to 1 year, and/or up to P30,000

Penalties go up to 2 years and 1 day to 3 years and/or up to P250,000 if the offense involves a syndicate, a business, a public officer, or 3 or more animals.
source: Republic Act No. 10631, Section 9 (formerly Section 8 of RA 8485), https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2013/ra_10631_2013.html

question: Where can I report animal abuse or neglect?
answer:
Under the Animal Welfare Act as amended by RA 10631 (Section 10):

- The Philippine National Police (PNP), the NBI and other law enforcement agencies have animal welfare enforcement officers
- The Secretary of Agriculture can deputize trained volunteers and members of NGOs and community groups as enforcement officers
- These officers can rescue maltreated animals and arrest violators

LGUs are also required to enforce the anti-cruelty rules of RA 8485 (RA 9482, Section 7). You can report to the police, your LGU, or an animal welfare group. Take photos or videos and note the date and place to help your report.
source: Republic Act No. 10631, Section 10, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2013/ra_10631_2013.html; Republic Act No. 9482, Section 7, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2007/ra_9482_2007.html

question: Can a pet legally be put to sleep in the Philippines?
answer:
Only for reasons the Animal Welfare Act allows. Section 6 of RA 8485 permits killing a pet when, for example:

- A licensed vet certifies it has an incurable communicable disease
- A licensed vet certifies it is needed to end the animal's suffering
- It is needed to prevent immediate danger to human life or limb

It must be done humanely, using methods approved by the Committee on Animal Welfare. Electrocution of dogs is banned under RA 9482. Talk to your vet if you're facing this decision.
source: Republic Act No. 8485, Section 6, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1998/ra_8485_1998.html; Republic Act No. 10631, Section 6, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2013/ra_10631_2013.html; Republic Act No. 9482, Sections 7 and 11, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2007/ra_9482_2007.html

question: What papers do I need to bring my dog or cat to another island or province?
answer:
You need a local shipping permit from the Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), applied for online at nvqsd.bai.gov.ph. Under the BAI Citizen's Charter, dogs and cats need:

- A veterinary health certificate from a licensed vet, showing rabies vaccine details (brand, batch/lot number, date given, next due date)
- A rabies vaccination certificate signed by the vet with their PRC number
- The pet should be about 3 to 4 months old or older
- The rabies shot should be at least 14 days and not more than 1 year old (annual boosters can ship right away)

The permit is free; processing takes up to 3 working days. Rules may change, so confirm with BAI before your trip.
source: BAI NVQSD Citizen's Charter, Service 8 (Local Shipping Permit), https://www.bai.gov.ph/cc/citizens%20charter%20(nvqsd).pdf; BAI One-Time Local Shipping Permit guide, https://nvqsd.bai.gov.ph/Admin/ONE%20TIME%20LOCAL%20PDF.pdf

question: Are there rules on how my pet should be transported, like by van or boat?
answer:
Yes. Section 4 of the Animal Welfare Act (RA 8485) sets rules for transporting animals:

- Carriers must provide clean, sanitary facilities for animals
- Animals must get food and water on trips longer than 12 hours, or when needed
- Overcrowding, cruel confinement and putting animals in vehicle trunks count as cruelty

A BAI permit is required to transport animals. For pets, apply for a BAI local shipping permit before your trip, and prepare a vet health certificate and rabies vaccination certificate.
source: Republic Act No. 8485, Section 4, https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1998/ra_8485_1998.html; BAI NVQSD Citizen's Charter, https://www.bai.gov.ph/cc/citizens%20charter%20(nvqsd).pdf
